intro.text: Founded in 1920, Helmerich & Payne, Inc. (H&P) (NYSE: HP) is committed to delivering industry leading levels of drilling productivity and reliability. H&P operates with the highest level of integrity, safety and innovation to deliver superior results for its customers and returns for shareholders. Through its subsidiaries, the Company designs, fabricates and operates high-performance drilling rigs in conventional and unconventional plays around the world. H&P also develops and implements advanced automation, directional drilling and survey management technologies. For more information, see H&P online at www.hpinc.com

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: We did not have any individual customers that represented 10% or more of our total consolidated revenues in fiscal year 2023.

As indicated in the accompanying Management’s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting, management’s assessment of and conclusion on the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting did not include the internal controls of KCA Deutag, which is included in the 2025 consolidated financial statements of the Company and constituted 38% of total identifiable assets as of September 30, 2025 and 27% of revenues for the year then ended.
In fiscal year 2023, no individual customers constituted 10 percent or more of our total consolidated revenues.

During the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025, approximately 33.8 percent of our operating revenues were generated from international locations compared to 7.2 percent during the fiscal year ended September 30, 2024.
During the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025, a single customer in Saudi Arabia accounted for 7.0 percent of our total consolidated operating revenues.
Our business largely depends on the level of capital spending by oil and gas companies for exploration and production activities.
Our business depends on the conditions of the land and offshore oil and natural gas industry.

Demand for our services and the rates we are able to charge for such services depend on oil and natural gas industry exploration and production activity and expenditure levels, which are directly affected by both long- and short-term trends in oil and natural gas prices and market expectations regarding such prices.
We greatly depend on the efforts of our executive officers and other key employees to manage our operations.

Since our business depends on the level of activity in the oil and natural gas industry, any improvement in or new discoveries of alternative energy technologies that increase the use of alternative forms of energy and reduce the demand for oil and natural gas could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Our ability to make future scheduled payments on or to refinance our debt obligations, including any future debt obligations, depends on our financial position, results of operations and cash flows.
Our ability to restructure or refinance our debt will depend on the condition of the capital markets and our financial position at such time.
Our ability to benefit from our deferred tax assets depends on us having sufficient future taxable income to utilize our net operating loss and tax credit carryforwards before they expire.

The declaration and amount of future dividends is at the discretion of our Board of Directors and will depend on our financial condition, results of operations, cash flows, prospects, industry conditions, capital requirements and other factors and restrictions our Board of Directors deems relevant.
Payment of future dividends will depend on earnings and other factors and is subject to Board approval.

Our ability to access the debt and equity capital markets depends on a number of factors, including our credit rating, market and industry conditions and market perceptions of our industry, general economic conditions, our revenue backlog and our capital expenditure commitments.

s.t: During the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025, we recorded a $ 29.6 million loss on our investment in Galileo, due to an allowance for credit loss on the convertible note, driven by heightened liquidity constraints and changes in governance, which led management to conclude that the fair value of the investment was not recoverable.
The aggregate loss primarily consisted of a $14.3 million loss on our investment in Tamboran due to changes in the fair value of the investment.
The aggregate loss was partially offset by a $6.7 million gain on our investment in Tamboran due to a change in the fair value of the investment.

The aggregate gain consisted of $15.0 million, $10.2 million, and $1.3 million of gains on various geothermal investments, our investment in Galileo, and our investment in Tamboran, respectively, due to changes in the fair value of the investments.
The gain was partially offset by a $12.4 million loss on our sale of equity investments in ADNOC Drilling.

Debt Securities During April 2022, the Company made a $ 33.0 million cornerstone investment in Galileo Holdco 2 Limited Technologies ("Galileo Holdco 2"), part of the group of companies known as Galileo Technologies (“Galileo”) in the form of notes with an option to convert into common shares of the parent of Galileo Holdco 2.

As of June 30, 2026, we owned approximately 1.0 million shares in Tamboran Corp. whose securities are traded on the NYSE and Australian Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol "TBN", representing an ownership interest of approximately 3.6 %.

s.t: The aggregate loss consisted primarily of a $29.6 million loss on our investment in Galileo, due to an allowance for credit loss on the convertible note, driven by heightened liquidity constraints and changes in governance, which led management to conclude that the fair value of the investment was not recoverable and a $12.4 million loss on our sale of equity securities in ADNOC Drilling, of which $8.4 million is associated with the change in the fair value of the investment and $4.0 million relates to transaction fees associated with the sale of the securities.

The loss was partially offset by $15.4 million and $5.0 million of gains on various geothermal equity investments and our investment in Tamboran, respectively, due to changes in the fair value of the investments.

Additionally, during the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025, we recorded a $ 29.6 million loss on our investment in Galileo, due to an allowance for credit loss on the convertible note, driven by heightened liquidity constraints and changes in governance, which led management to conclude that the fair value of the investment was not recoverable.

Our activity during the fiscal year ended September 30, 2023, was driven by purchases of a $14.1 million equity investment in Tamboran Resources Corporation, $4.1 million in debt and equity security investments in various geothermal energy companies, and $2.5 million investments in other equity securities.
In October 2022, we made a $14.1 million equity investment, representing 106.0 million common shares in Tamboran Resources.

On June 26, 2024, Tamboran Corp. completed an initial public offering of its common stock on the NYSE and as a result of this offering, our convertible note of $9.4 million was converted into 0.5 million common shares in Tamboran Corp.

As a result of this offering, the convertible note of $ 9.4 million was converted into 0.5 million common shares in Tamboran Corp. During the fiscal year ended September 30, 2025, our representation on the investee’s board of directors ceased.

To finance the purchase price and to pay related fees and expenses, we completed a private offering of $ 1.25 billion aggregate principal amount of senior notes, together with the proceeds of a term loan credit agreement, cash on hand, and monetization of our investment in ADNOC Drilling.

During September 2021, the Company made a $ 100.0 million cornerstone investment in ADNOC Drilling in advance of its announced initial public offering, representing 159.7 million shares of ADNOC Drilling, equivalent to a one percent ownership stake and subject to a three-year lockup period.
Equity Securities with Fair Value Option In October 2022, we made a $ 14.1 million equity investment, representing 106.0 million common shares in Tamboran Resources.

As a result of this offering, the convertible note of $ 9.4 million was converted into 0.5 million common shares in Tamboran Corp. Our shares received in this initial public offering were subject to a 180-day lockup period, which expired during the first fiscal quarter of 2025.

Debt Securities During April 2022, the Company made a $ 33.0 million cornerstone investment in Galileo Holdco 2 Limited Technologies ("Galileo Holdco 2"), part of the group of companies known as Galileo Technologies (“Galileo”) in the form of notes with an option to convert into common shares of the parent of Galileo Holdco 2.

This gain consisted primarily of $30.9 million and $1.6 million gains on our equity investment in ADNOC Drilling and Tamboran Corp; both of which were a result of increases in the fair market values of the stocks.

The gains on our equity investments in ADNOC Drilling and Tamboran Corp. during the fiscal year ended September 30, 2024 were offset by a $10.2 million and $1.4 million of losses on our investments in Galileo and a geothermal equity security, respectively, due to changes in the fair values of the investments, and a $7.1 million loss as a result of a Blue Chip Swap transaction.

The cash consideration was funded through a combination of net proceeds from the Company’s September 2024 senior notes offering, net proceeds from the funding of the Company’s Term Loan Credit Agreement, cash on hand, and monetization of our investment in ADNOC Drilling.

The decrease primarily reflects the liquidation of our investment in ADNOC Drilling during the year ended September 30, 2025, which resulted in no dividend income for the period compared to $11.1 million in dividend income recognized during the year ended 2024, partially offset to high market interest rates in fiscal year 2025.

On June 4, 2024, the Company entered into a convertible note agreement with Tamboran Corp. This note was utilized to relieve Tamboran's outstanding accounts receivable balance owed to the Company, and therefore no cash was exchanged as part of the transaction.
Concurrent with the October 2022 investment agreement, we entered into a fixed-term drilling services agreement with Tamboran Resources.

A majority of our long-term debt securities, including our investment in Galileo, are classified as available-for-sale and are measured using Level 3 unobservable inputs based on the absence of market activity.
